dhp157:3:
The wise person would stay awake
nursing himself
dhp157:4:
in any of the three watches of the night,
the three stages of life.
dhp158:4:
only then
teach others.
He wouldn’t stain his name
: he is wise.
dhp160:1:
Your own self is
your own mainstay,
dhp160:2: for who else could your mainstay be?
dhp160:4:
you obtain the mainstay
hard to obtain.
dhp161:1: The evil he himself has done
dhp161:4: as a diamond, a precious stone.
dhp162:2: like a sal tree by a vine–
dhp163:2:
things of no good
& no use to yourself.
dhp163:4: is truly harder than hard to do.
dhp164:1: The teaching of those who live the Dhamma,
dhp164:5: bears fruit for his own destruction,
dhp164:6: like the fruiting of the bamboo.
dhp165:3:
Evil is left undone
by oneself,
dhp165:5: Purity & impurity are one’s own doing.
dhp165:6:
No one purifies another.
No other purifies one.
dhp166:2:
for that of another,
no matter how great.
